_comment: Patient portals, and what we know about getting a full record out of each.
TO ADD OR CORRECT ONE: edit this file and open a pull request. You do not
need to know JavaScript. Copy an existing block, change the values, keep the
commas and braces where they are.
- 'status' is 'verified' only if someone actually did it end to end.
Otherwise 'unknown'. Do not guess a menu path you have not seen.
- Describe how the SYSTEM behaves. Never anything about a person's health.
- 'steps' are what a non-technical person clicks, in order.
- Leave 'steps' empty when unknown. Empty is honest; invented is not.

providers.name: MyChart
providers.aka: Used by most large US hospital systems. If your portal is called MyChart, or your hospital's own name plus 'Chart', this is it.
providers.format: A .zip file containing C-CDA XML documents
steps: Sign in to your hospital's MyChart website. If you have records at more than one hospital system, you will need to do this once for each.
Open the menu and look for 'Document Center'. Inside it, choose 'Requested Records'.
Choose to request your full record. Some hospitals label this 'Visit Records' or 'Download My Record'.
Ask for all visits, or the widest date range offered, rather than a single appointment.
The file is not ready immediately. It can take minutes or hours. You may get an email or a message in the portal when it is done.
Come back and download the .zip file. Save it somewhere you will find again.
warnings: The download link expires, often after about a week. Download it promptly and keep the file.

providers.aka: Common at independent and mid-size practices.

providers.name: My HealtheVet
warnings: The VA has a long-standing feature called Blue Button for downloading your record. That is the most likely path, but nobody has confirmed the details here yet.

providers.name: Something else, or I don't know
providers.aka: Pick this if your portal is not listed, or you are not sure which one you have.
